feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the scope feels substantial. It reads polished and modern, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less duplication across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”  
- Good credibility and scope: large-scale Drupal migration, analytics stack expansion, studio buildout, and AI search project all signal meaningful ownership.  
- Writing is generally clean and professional, with strong action verbs and relevant public-sector context.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings, search improvement, campaign performance).  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating would improve scannability and structure.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: mixed punctuation and list formatting, inconsistent use of commas/serial commas, and some awkward phrasing (“A2/Learning” → “A2 (learning)”; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary). No obvious misspellings, but minor stylistic inconsistencies make the document feel slightly overpacked.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It aligns well with the CV, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and make the value proposition more direct: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for public-sector and mission-driven organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with simpler, more active phrasing such as “leading web modernization, digital governance, and content operations.”
- Consider adding one concrete scale marker from recent experience for impact, e.g., “10,000+ page websites” or “high-volume platforms serving millions of annual page views.”
- Streamline the service list to 3–4 priority areas: web modernization, analytics/reporting, editorial governance, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The long capability list repeats content already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less overlapping capability areas and phrased more consistently.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and use parallel noun phrases; e.g. “Enterprise web modernization and CMS governance” instead of splitting modernization/governance/editorial systems.
- Replace generic terms like “operations” and “infrastructure” with sharper outcomes-oriented language such as “performance analytics and executive reporting” or “cross-channel content operations.”
- Prioritize most marketable recent strengths first: web modernization, governance/CMS, analytics, AI search, automation/integrations.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization and CMS governance • Editorial systems and content operations • Performance analytics and executive reporting • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream delivery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with Recent Projects and Topline Skills.
- Multimedia, analytics, governance, and multi-channel communications are already covered in both the header and Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies. Tightening the language and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinct and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” to reinforce recency and frame this as a portfolio-style addendum.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: “Built,” “Led,” “Developed,” “Launched,” and trim stacked nouns like “structured content workflows.”
- Add one concrete detail per project where possible: audience, platform, scale, or business outcome.
- Consider rewrite: “Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider keeping only the most differentiated 2–3 projects here.

items.title: Coleman Davis
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around outcomes, scale, and what is new at this senior level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate execution bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; combine CMS/front-end/troubleshooting into one line and foreground enterprise value.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users/members reached, workflow time reduced, campaign launches delivered, search/discovery improvements, stakeholder teams enabled.
- Rephrase AI/search bullet to show ownership and business value: “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Custom microsite structures” and “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consulting scope, embedded leadership, and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals; it will be stronger if you tighten the opening and make outcomes more explicit. Emphasize transformation, team/channel ownership, and business impact rather than listing every responsibility.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Recast bullets to lead with outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: growth in email engagement, social reach, video output, production savings, reporting speed, or governance adoption.
- Tighten wording: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting stack.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video/programming leadership overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on scaling/building the studio, not recurring video production.
- Editorial workflow/governance language overlaps with the consultant role; distinguish this as enterprise leadership inside one organization.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid mid-career progression item, but it reads as a bridge between the older producer role and the later director role. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and operational improvements without repeating website, analytics, or studio achievements covered in the 2022–2024 role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Strengthen bullets with action + outcome: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders” and, if possible, add open rates, growth, or engagement lift.
- Reframe video bullet to show ownership: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one more concise operations bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and speed of digital output.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating website migration, analytics infrastructure, or governance language already covered more strongly in the Director role.
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; here, stress expansion/operationalization rather than initial production.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the leadership scope and emphasize the most current, high-value strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, more distinctive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “AI-enabled content discovery” if you want this section to better reflect recent consulting work.
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid broad terms like “leadership” twice across nearby sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also echoes the header and multiple NACo roles; tighten or replace if space is limited.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths rather than listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters tied to recent work: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older items here, especially jQuery, unless it is central to current target roles.
- Consider replacing “Power Pages” and possibly “SharePoint” with a broader phrase like “enterprise web platforms” if those platforms are not supported by recent experience bullets.
- Keep this section concise; let the “Technical + IT” section carry the full software inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly all items duplicate the “Technical + IT” section; avoid repeating exact platform lists in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies and recent project content.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capability and decision impact rather than repeat platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to outcome-oriented skill cluster, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools and combine the rest: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten phrasing to show business use: “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” “SEO and digital performance analysis,” “insight-driven optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis • Insight-driven optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating every analytics tool here if they already appear in the Technical + IT section.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and oriented to operational delivery rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task-level to leadership-level language: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • In-house studio operations • Virtual event production”
- If space allows, sharpen impact with scope-oriented phrasing: “Broadcast-quality in-house video and livestream production” to echo the studio build without repeating full job details.
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” or “Video production, editing and distribution” only if distribution is not covered elsewhere.
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools, formats, and environments inconsistently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations”; vary wording or remove one.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already supported by recent NACo experience, so don’t over-explain them here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section above. This item should either be tightened or reframed to emphasize depth/relevance, especially Drupal and enterprise CMS work.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize most relevant platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal site building/microsites • WordPress • SharePoint intranet/content admin • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep phrasing consistent with other technical lists; avoid implying equal depth across all tools if Drupal is clearly the strongest.
- If this section is meant to show hands-on capability, consider renaming to “CMS Platforms” for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; consider merging or using one section for platforms and the other for broader capabilities.
- Drupal is already heavily evidenced in recent roles/projects, so avoid overloading multiple sections with the same platform list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from broad coding languages to applied delivery: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/jQuery”
- Group modern tooling by use case: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome language elsewhere or in a parenthetical here, e.g., “for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless needed; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one version shorter or make this one more implementation-focused
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless tagging implementation is a core technical differentiator

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and reads like an undifferentiated software list. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this section should be tighter and more clearly organized around systems you actively used in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to improve signal: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/Workflow Management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first based on recent work; if Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier were central to building workflows, lead with those.
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools” so Slack/Teams fit naturally.
- If possible, replace generic listing with light proficiency framing: “Built workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; managed delivery in Jira/Asana/Trello.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they were materially important to cross-team operations.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for this profile, but the line is too bare to show depth or seniority. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS matching: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one capability cue instead of more tools: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • newsletter operations / audience journeys
- Keep this as a simple stack list; let work experience carry outcomes like audience size, newsletter volume, and campaign leadership

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or campaign management claims here; those are already covered in NACo experience
- “Engagement” overlaps with Core Competencies’ multi-channel communications, so don’t broaden this into social or advocacy platforms

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, make it tighter and more implementation-focused, with methods grouped under tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/reporting dashboards
- Replace broad “SEO” with a more concrete platform/process term like “Google Search Console” or “SEO analysis” if that’s what you actually used.
- Change “Dashboarding” to “KPI/reporting dashboards” or “executive reporting dashboards” to sound more outcome-oriented.
- Order by strongest/recent tools first: GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, then optimization methods.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This line substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one or using this section for tools only and the topline section for capabilities.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating extra descriptors here unless they add specificity.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this role clearly foundational: team build-out, early platform/content wins, and light people support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function.”
- Tighten responsibilities into 2–3 concrete outcomes: website refresh support, recurring livestream/video production, and workflow improvements across web/email/social.
- Replace vague phrases like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with specifics or metrics if available (e.g., number of livestreams, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, production volume).
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, improved day-to-day publishing workflows across web, email and social, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates. Also provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate as launch/build phase here.
- Avoid repeating broad channel ownership already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/program support and the first-podcast launch.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities; partnered across teams to turn findings into usable communications assets.”
- Tighten the digital piece to one concrete line: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational campaigns and program communications.”
- Make the podcast achievement sharper: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add scale or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize multimedia leadership here; later positions show a clearer progression in video/studio ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mixed capabilities bucket than a clean tools line. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in work experience and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
